name: AI agents
blurb: Agents, tools and MCP servers that actually work: scoping, tool design, multi-agent, memory, evals, Claude and other stacks.
searches: MCP specification new release server features
Claude Agent SDK managed agents new feature
agent tool design best practices evaluation
agent skill MCP server Claude Code new

tests.prompt: I want Claude to work with our internal ticketing REST API (about 40 endpoints, OAuth 2.0). Plan the MCP server: deployment model, tool list, auth, and how you'll test it. Then write the TypeScript for the two most-used tools.
tests.good: Recommends a remote streamable-HTTP server; search+execute or a hybrid with 3-5 promoted tools given 40 endpoints; reads and writes separate with readOnly/destructive annotations; OAuth via CIMD or DCR with audience validation and no token passthrough; Zod schemas with described params, pagination and actionable isError messages; Inspector test plus a 10-question read-only eval.

tests.prompt: Every Monday I copy last week's Stripe refunds into a spreadsheet and email a summary to finance. Should this be an agent? Design the first version.
tests.good: Runs the agent-vs-workflow check and likely picks a scheduled workflow or a small agent with a clear rationale; defines trigger (cron + timezone), tools, never-dos (no sending without approval in v0, drafts or mocked outbox), 3-6 binary done-checks, a v1/v2 list with reasons, no hard-coded dates in the scheduled prompt, and an eval/verification step.

tests.prompt: Our research agent gets worse the longer it runs and sometimes contradicts itself. We are thinking of splitting it into five sub-agents. What would you do?
tests.good: Diagnoses context degradation first (stale tool output, no compaction/clearing, big pasted docs) and fixes that; considers memory/validity issues for contradictions; only then proposes sub-agents for independent parts with self-contained briefs, short return schemas and shared files, capped worker count and budgets; insists on measuring against a single-agent baseline with an eval set.

tests.prompt: Build a remote MCP server so our support team can search, read and update tickets through our helpdesk's REST API from Claude. Host it on Cloudflare Workers, keep the helpdesk API key out of the code, and show me the tools work before we roll it out.
tests.good: States a short plan first: agent-or-workflow.md, tool-design.md, mcp-servers.md and evaluation.md here; hosting through cloud-devops (cloudflare.md: Wrangler, the key set with wrangler secret put, never in config); the key and abuse paths through security (secrets.md, threat-modeling.md: injected ticket text, who may update what). Separate read and write tools with readOnlyHint and destructiveHint; updates gated behind confirmation; OAuth with audience checks and no token passthrough; actionable errors and pagination; an Inspector smoke test and a read-only 10-question eval; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Build me a support-triage agent in Python with the OpenAI Agents SDK. A triage agent should hand off to a billing agent and a technical agent. Billing has a refund tool that must not run without a human saying yes. Add a guardrail that stops obvious prompt-injection in the customer's message, send traces to Langfuse, and give me a small eval with 8 test tickets, 3 of them kept back.
tests.good: Uses current Agents SDK APIs: Agent with handoffs, Runner.run with a max_turns limit, @function_tool, input guardrail with tripwire; checks the installed version and lists models live instead of guessing IDs.|Refund is a separate write tool gated by an approval step enforced in code (needs-approval or confirmation tool), with refund amount capped and typed; no auto-run.|Injection guardrail and system prompt treat ticket text as data; tool results are not obeyed.|Langfuse tracing via its OpenAI Agents integration or OpenTelemetry, with keys read from environment variables, .env git-ignored, nothing printed or hardcoded.|Eval has binary checks (right handoff, refund not issued without approval, injection blocked), scored separately, with 3 cases held back and not used while tuning.|Does one real run on a sample ticket and shows its output; states what is mocked (refund API) and what is left for v1.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK and Claude API tool use
tools.why: Default way to build agents on Claude: Messages API tool loop, Agent SDK (Python/TS, 8.2k stars on the Python repo) and Managed Agents.

tools.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP) SDKs and Inspector
tools.why: The standard tool-connection protocol across Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others; Python SDK 24k stars, TS SDK 13k, Inspector 11k on GitHub.

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.why: Python SDK 29.8k stars and about 10M monthly downloads, named among the most adopted frameworks in Firecrawl and LangChain round-ups.

tools.name: LangGraph and LangChain (Deep Agents)
tools.why: Leads enterprise adoption (43% of orgs per a 2026 round-up, 34M monthly downloads); LangChain's State of Agent Engineering report is the main practitioner survey.

tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
tools.why: The default TypeScript toolkit for LLM apps and agents (vercel/ai 27k stars); tool loops, MCP client and React hooks.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.why: About 49k GitHub stars and a claimed 60% of Fortune 500 users; listed in every 2026 framework round-up.

tools.name: Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen, Semantic Kernel)
tools.why: Microsoft's merged successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, 13.9k stars, in the Firecrawl and LangChain round-ups; default for .NET and Azure shops.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.why: Tracing, datasets and evals for the LangChain stack; one of the big four platforms in 2026 observability round-ups.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.why: Open-source leader for LLM tracing, prompts and evals (35k stars, acquired by ClickHouse in 2026); 'safest default' in the MarkTechPost and Firecrawl round-ups.

tools.name: Pydantic AI
tools.why: Type-safe Python agent framework, 20k stars, named among leading frameworks in 2026 comparisons.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.why: Leading RAG and document-agent framework, 52k stars.

tools.name: AWS Strands Agents and Bedrock AgentCore
tools.why: AWS's open-source agent SDK (8.7k stars) and managed runtime; the default choice for agents on AWS.

tools.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
tools.why: Google's agent framework with A2A; agents-cli repo 6k stars; in 2026 round-ups.

tools.name: Mastra
tools.why: Leading TypeScript agent framework, 28.5k stars.

tools.name: promptfoo
tools.why: Most-used open-source eval and red-team CLI (25.7k stars); recommended for first CI eval gate in 2026 round-ups.

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
tools.why: Microsoft's low-code agent builder (agents, agent flows, tools, MCP and custom connectors, evaluations, publishing to Teams/M365 Copilot/web); Microsoft says 90% of Fortune 500 companies use it, making it the most widely deployed enterprise agent builder.

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.why: Eval and tracing platform used by Notion, Airtable, Stripe and Vercel; raised $80M at an $800M valuation in Feb 2026 and is one of the four platforms every 2026 observability round-up compares (MarkTechPost, Aug 2026).

tools.name: Arize Phoenix
tools.why: Open-source, OpenTelemetry-based tracing and eval platform (11.7k stars); Arize reports ~50M evaluations a month and over 1 trillion spans logged, one of the big four in 2026 observability comparisons.

tools.name: ElevenLabs Agents Platform
tools.why: The router's own voice-agent stack; ElevenLabs raised $500M at an $11B valuation (Feb 2026) and leads voice-agent comparisons on voice quality and latency.

tools.name: LiveKit Agents
tools.why: Open-source realtime framework (Python/Node) for voice and video agents and the code-first default behind many production voice agents; LiveKit raised $100M at a $1B valuation in Jan 2026.

tools.name: Vapi
tools.why: Developer platform for phone voice agents; named with ElevenLabs and Retell as the market's leaders in 2026 comparisons, raised $50M at ~$500M after winning Amazon Ring.

tools.name: OpenAI ChatGPT Plugins (Apps SDK)
tools.why: OpenAI's SDK for putting an MCP server with UI widgets and skills inside ChatGPT (the Apps SDK, now documented as Plugins; ChatKit stays while Agent Builder retires on 30 Nov 2026); the second big host for MCP apps.

tools.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
tools.why: Stateful agents on Workers and Durable Objects (memory, WebSockets, schedules, remote MCP); named in the router and covered in frameworks.md, with an official Cloudflare skill.
